findings.title: Task 2.2 and design D3 carry only the retired trigger's notice, not the flag handling or the mid-walk switch the spec now requires
findings.recommendation: The walk's F4 fix rewrote `Every walk runs finding by finding` (specs/orbit-address-reviews/spec.md:177): `--batch` is dropped before discovery resolves the positional, the retired verbal forms are named, and a bare mid-walk 'go batch' / 'switch to batch' / 'batch the rest' is read as a delegation recorded verbatim as delegation_directive. Neither the tasks nor the design followed: task 2.2 still says only 'add the one-line notice for a retired trigger', and design D3 says only that the delegation directive stays. An apply built to the tasks writes the notice and never the flag handling or the delegation reading, so the new scenario 'A retired mid-walk switch is a delegation' would have no body text behind it. A second consequence: the body will now NAME the retired phrases ('--batch', 'fix them all', 'go batch', 'batch the rest'), so the cut ledger's `removed` pairs for batch mode must take their phrase from text that leaves entirely (`walk_mode_source`, `command-shape-interruption`, 'Batch-mode is opt-in'), or their phrase check fails by construction. Widen task 2.2 and design D3 with both points.

walk_entry.title: A command-shaped mid-walk batch switch ("go batch", "batch the rest") has no specified behaviour once batch mode is removed

findings.title: Design D3 still says a new log always carries per_finding, which the spec's new named limit contradicts
findings.recommendation: The walk's F6 fix named the limit in `Every walk runs finding by finding`: the rules govern what the walk writes, and the write gate checks neither walk_mode's value nor a per-resolution disagreement. Design D3 (design.md:107) still says `walk_mode` stays required and 'a new log always carries "per_finding"', an overclaim against that limit. Say 'a log the walk writes carries "per_finding"; the write gate does not check the value (the named limit in the spec)'.

walk_entry.title: Task 2.2 lists only some of the schema reference's batch and disagreement text

findings.title: A Risks bullet still describes moved pairs by their first line
findings.recommendation: The walk's E5 fix made a `moved` pair name its span by start and end anchors with a digest of the text before the move. The Risks bullet at design.md:226 still reads 'every moved section's first line and every reworded span' and 'Moves store no text'. Reword it to 'every moved span's two anchors and digest, and every reworded or removed span; moves store anchors and a digest, never the moved text'.

walk_entry.title: The cut ledger cannot reliably identify the bytes it must restore

commentary: Graded the two walks of the proposal pair over each owed entry's sweep scope, then ran the nine passes over the union, the whole change directory and the program doc. The residual range from the external return's adding commit lists seven files, every one inside some entry's edit record, so no record gap. The pattern is the one these verifications usually find: each regression is a fix that landed in the spec or the design table and stopped one artifact short, in the tasks or in a prose sentence elsewhere in the design. The F4 gap is the one that would change what apply builds; the other two are wording. orbit validate --strict passes with INFO only and no @review: marker remains.
